newsitem.title: FRANCE: Prodi says will use all means to join euro - paper.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says will use all means to join euro - paper.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister was quoted as saying Italy would use all political instruments at its disposal to ensure that Italy takes part in a single European currency at the scheduled start in 1999.

In an interview to appear in Tuesday's La Tribune, Prodi also said no exchange rate mechanism, or ERM II, for countries outside the euro zone would be able to control events if the lira were not part of the single currency.

"No follow on ERM will prevent the fact that events will be impossible to control if the lira is not in the euro," Prodi was quoted as saying. He said that for ERM II to work there would have to be a policy of solidarity.

"But what solidarity is conceivable in the case of a fight?...in the event of a negative decision against Italy on the euro, the context would be more one of hostility than cooperation," Prodi said. The participation of Spain and Portugal was just as important as Italy's, but if Italy were excluded from the euro initially, "Italy is determined to use all politicial instruments at its disposal."

Prodi said the current level of the lira was satisfying and did not pose any problems from the point of view of competitivity and, as inflation was no longer higher than that in competing countries, the level was also sustainable.
He repeated his conviction that Italy would respect the strict three percent Maastricht treaty criterion for public deficits as a percentage of gross domestic product in 1997.

"I have the conviction that Europe without Italy would not be Europe. But it will not be necessary to interpret the critieria as I have no doubt we will respect the three percent public deficit criterion," Prodi said.
He said Italy was counting on respecting the Maastricht agreement by having a stable public deficit outlook.
But he said: "It will be difficult to go significantly below three percent" in 1998.
He said the government would try to find a "good mix" of exceptional and structural measures for its 1998 budget.
